# SEO-448: Detect thin location pages generated from a template

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `local` |
| Category | `CONTENT_QUALITY` |
| Minimum level | `RECOMMENDED` |
| Severity | `HIGH` |
| Impact | `HIGH` |
| Change safety | `BLOCKED` |
| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

Routes produced by substituting a place name into a shared template, with no content specific to that place, are reported as a defect rather than as coverage, and no such route is generated by this process.

## Rationale

Pages differing only by a place name exist to catch queries rather than to serve the person who arrives, which is the pattern search platforms document as disallowed.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site",
    "local_business"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Compare location routes against each other and report clusters whose text is identical apart from substituted place names. Consolidate them into the pages that describe real places, and never expand the set.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Extract body text from every location route, measure pairwise similarity after removing place names, and report clusters above the reporting threshold.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `ROUTE`, `MANUAL_ACTION`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `LOCAL_SEARCH`, `GOOGLE_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: The cited policy describes this pattern as disallowed, so generating such pages is out of scope for this process under any instruction. Consolidating existing ones removes published addresses, which is why the change is not automatic.
